questions.text: Which comparison best distinguishes Yajurveda and Samaveda in a basic Veda overview?

options.label: A
options.text: Yajurveda is associated with ritual formulas; Samaveda with chants/melodies

options.label: B
options.text: Yajurveda is metre; Samaveda is grammar

options.label: C
options.text: Yajurveda is a Purana; Samaveda is a Vedanga

options.label: D
options.text: Both are types of temple architecture

questions.rationale: This is the standard broad distinction between the two Vedas.

questions.text: A local-history project considers water management and trade connections. Which pair of topics fits the syllabus?
questions.rationale: The syllabus includes both water systems and trading/transportation themes.

questions.text: A team describes a site as showing 'urban planning' but gives only a photograph with no scale, date or site context. What is the main limitation?

options.label: A
options.text: The evidence is insufficient to support a detailed historical interpretation

options.label: B
options.text: The photo proves the site's exact date

options.label: C
options.text: Urban planning is not a syllabus topic

options.label: D
options.text: A photograph alone gives all design rules

questions.rationale: A photograph without context cannot support precise historical conclusions.

questions.text: An ethical-living presentation needs to include duty, prosperity, enjoyment and liberation. What structure avoids omitting any Purushartha?
questions.rationale: These are the four Purusharthas.

questions.text: A student's notes define Jyotisha as poetic metre and Chandas as calendar study. Which correction is needed?

options.label: A
options.text: Jyotisha relates to astronomy/timekeeping; Chandas studies metre

options.label: B
options.text: Jyotisha is grammar; Chandas is metalworking

options.label: C
options.text: Jyotisha is a Veda; Chandas is a Purana

questions.rationale: Jyotisha and Chandas have distinct fields.

questions.text: A case study tries to show that a particular reservoir reflects historical water-management knowledge. What is the strongest evidence plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Combine site-specific records or credible studies with analysis of storage, supply and setting

options.label: B
options.text: Use only the modern name of the reservoir

options.label: C
options.text: Assume every reservoir belongs to the same tradition

options.label: D
options.text: Infer details solely from the general syllabus

questions.rationale: Specific claims require case-specific evidence and analysis.

questions.text: A student wants to compare four Vedas, six Vedangas and four other branches without mixing categories. What is the correct count check?
questions.rationale: The conventional grouping totals fourteen knowledge branches.

questions.text: A presentation links traditional measurement with modern scientific units. Which method is strongest?

options.label: A
options.text: Define each unit, identify its historical/source context and state any conversion assumptions

options.label: B
options.text: Treat every historical unit as exactly one modern unit without evidence

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore whether units measure time, distance or weight

questions.rationale: Comparisons require definitions, context and explicit conversion assumptions.

questions.text: A team is asked to discuss a temple's form through the syllabus's architecture themes. Which topics are most directly relevant?

options.label: A
options.text: Vastu Shastra, civil architecture and temple architecture

options.label: B
options.text: NLP, HTML forms and email signatures

questions.rationale: The architecture unit names Vastu, civil architecture and temple architecture.

questions.text: An argument claims Moksha is simply a synonym for material prosperity. What is the best correction?

options.label: A
options.text: Moksha refers to liberation; Artha is the Purushartha associated with material means

options.label: B
options.text: Moksha is grammar and Artha is metre

questions.rationale: Moksha and Artha denote distinct aims.

questions.text: A researcher has evidence about textile dyeing from one site but wants to describe all ancient India. What wording is best?

options.label: A
options.text: This site provides an example of textile dyeing practice; broader prevalence needs additional evidence

options.label: B
options.text: All places used precisely the same technique

options.label: C
options.text: The site proves a universal rule

questions.rationale: A specific case should not be generalized beyond its evidence.

questions.text: A student must describe the life-stage model but accidentally includes Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. What is the correction?

options.label: A
options.text: Those are Purusharthas; Ashramas are Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa

questions.rationale: Purusharthas are aims; Ashramas are life stages.

questions.text: A project compares the role of calendars with agriculture-related star knowledge. What is the most relevant topic pair?
questions.rationale: Both topics appear in the provided outline.

questions.text: A student wants to distinguish a supported syllabus fact from a historical hypothesis. Which practice is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Label the syllabus fact clearly and cite independent, case-specific evidence for the hypothesis

options.label: B
options.text: Treat every hypothesis as verified because it fits the theme

options.label: D
options.text: Use confidence of wording as evidence

questions.rationale: The course outline indicates coverage but doesn't verify every particular historical claim.

questions.text: Which conclusion best reflects the full range of the BKS course described in the source?

options.label: A
options.text: It spans textual and philosophical traditions, science/mathematics and technology/architecture

options.label: B
options.text: It is limited to rituals and excludes scientific topics

options.label: C
options.text: It is only a construction course

options.label: D
options.text: It is only a language grammar course

questions.rationale: The verified source covers all those broad knowledge areas.
